lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Wren Hollow, the night after the big storm.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Well, that's that. The old tower came down in the wind, and every radio went quiet.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: No weather, no news, no Radio Wren. Forty years on air, and not a peep tonight.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So we build it back up?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The big one takes time. We start small. Little towers, house by house.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: By Starfall Night, every home in the Hollow hears us again. Deal, apprentice?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Here's Main Street. See the dark windows? Those folks can't hear a thing.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Set a tower on the grass. Its signal reaches about two tiles all round.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And every house in reach lights up?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Every one. Light them all and the street is back on air.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Was that Radio Wren on my kitchen set? Splendid. Simply splendid!

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Nell, the council is fretting. They say the Hollow can't wait forever for news.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Tell the council they'll have it. My apprentice is quick.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Then Starfall Night stays on the calendar. All of it on air. No pressure!

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Look at that. The old tower, standing again, and Main Street all lit up.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Every window. Even the bakery.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Mrs. Tull's been baking by candlelight all week. Expect scones.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Now, someone up the hill has been waiting for us. Quietly.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Oh! Hello. Sorry, I whisper. Habit. I'm Juniper. I run the observatory.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: My telescopes listen to the sky. Your radio is lovely, but it is very loud to them.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: So the observatory stays out of every tower's reach. Not one can touch it.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Walls and hills make good shade. Starfall is coming, and I can't miss it.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Listen. Nothing at all. Just stars. It's perfect.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: The Wrenfall comes every autumn. Hundreds of meteors, right over the Hollow.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And on Starfall Night, everyone watches?

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Everyone listens. Radio Wren calls out every one. Well, it used to.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: It will again.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Welcome downtown! Phones ringing, kettles boiling, everyone talking at once!

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: But if one signal flickers, the whole office drops the call. Chaos!

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Then each office block gets two different towers. If one blinks, the other holds.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Two lamps on the roof for two signals. I like it. Very official.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Not a single dropped call all morning. The council is speechless!

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Well, they're talking a great deal, actually. But happily.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Good. Because the orchard farms past the ridge still hear nothing.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: The orchards? That's a long way out. You'll need something with real reach.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Found her in the shed. My old dish. She reaches far, but only one way.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Only one way?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: A quarter turn of sky, straight out. Tap her to turn her. Turning costs nothing.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Out here the little towers won't carry far. Let the dish do the long work.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: The orchard farms are on! I can hear them cheering from here.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: That's the Pell family. Loud lot. Bless them.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Now for the real test. I'm switching the old station back on.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: From here on, towers carry the real broadcast. Hand to hand.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Radio Wren station, back on the air. Forty years, and she still hums.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The station is a tower too. But the others must hear it to pass it on.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So every tower has to link back to the station, through other live towers?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Right. A tower with no link is just a pole in a field. No voice at all.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: I built the first tower on that hill with my dad. I was younger than you.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Did he teach you all this?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Most of it. Storms taught me the rest. Good teachers. Rude, though.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Hear that? That's the real Radio Wren, in every corner of town.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Nell! The Glass Lanes are still dark. The streets bend too much for signal.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: But I have spare telescope mirrors. Big ones. They bounce anything.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Mirrors. Juniper, you're a genius.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: I know. I mean, thank you.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Here they are. Polished panels from the old telescope. Mind the shine.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: A panel blocks signal head-on, but bounces it once, around the corner.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The bounce counts the whole trip, there and on. So stand close to the panel.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: One bounce, round the corner. Got it.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: That's the last dark street. The Glass Lanes are glowing.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: The panels catch the starlight too. Look. The whole lane sparkles.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Nell! Apprentice! Starfall Night is tomorrow. Is the Hollow ready?

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Almost. One last broadcast. Everything at once.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Bunting up, lanterns lit, cocoa on. The whole Hollow is out in the square!

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: And the observatory still needs quiet skies. The meteors start at nine.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Offices want two signals. The observatory wants none. Mind them both.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Everything you've learned, apprentice. One night. Let's go.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: First meteor! Did you see it? Right over the ridge!

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: I heard it! On the radio! That's how it's done!

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Two more streets, apprentice. Then the whole Hollow hears the show.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: This is Radio Wren, live from the hill. Starfall Night has begun.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Meteor at the ridge. Two by the orchard. Oh, there's a bright one!

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: Every house is listening. Every single one. The council is in tears!

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: We did it, Nell.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: You did it. I just held the ladder.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Starfall Night, Wren Hollow. Every window warm. Every radio on.

lines.speaker: otto
lines.text: The council voted this morning. Radio Wren stays on air. Forever, I told them.

lines.speaker: juniper
lines.text: Three hundred and twelve meteors. My best count ever, and not one buzz.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: I've been thinking. The Hollow needs a signal keeper. A proper one.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The tower's yours, keeper. Keep it humming.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Thank you for playing Signal Tower.

levelLines.1: The first window glows. Someone waves a tea towel.
levelLines.2: The garden wall kept the signal out. Not anymore.
levelLines.3: The house behind the hill hears the weather again.
levelLines.4: From the hilltop, the signal rolls all the way down.
levelLines.5: The cottages in the woods are humming along.
levelLines.6: The quarry workers' radio crackles back to life.
levelLines.7: The crossing guard hears the school report.
levelLines.8: Both sides of the long fence are on air.
levelLines.9: One valley, two halves, one station.
levelLines.10: Nine farmhouses on the back roads, all tuned in.
levelLines.11: The ridge cottages hear the evening songs.
levelLines.12: Every pocket of the maze is listening.
levelLines.13: Bigger towers, bigger reach. Main Street is buzzing.
levelLines.14: Even the old walled lane has news tonight.
levelLines.15: The old tower stands again. The Hollow cheers.
levelLines.17: Houses lit, telescope undisturbed. Juniper sighs.
levelLines.19: The hill keeps the deep field dark and still.
levelLines.20: Two lamps on the roof. The phones never drop.
levelLines.21: The day shift and the night shift both get through.
levelLines.22: The office works late, and so does the signal.
levelLines.23: Downtown hums. Otto says "splendid" six times.
levelLines.24: The dish finds the first orchard farm.
levelLines.25: One narrow beam, one very happy farmer.
levelLines.26: Signal flies down the long lane to the barns.
levelLines.27: Two dishes, aimed true. The orchards are on air.
levelLines.28: Station to tower, tower to home. The chain holds.
levelLines.29: A quiet tower in the middle carries the voice.
levelLines.30: Hill to hill, the broadcast steps across town.
levelLines.31: From the corner station to the far side of town.
levelLines.32: The signal turns its first corner.
levelLines.33: A lane that never had signal hears music.
levelLines.34: Two sealed gardens, both reached by a bounce.
levelLines.35: The Glass Lanes sparkle and sing.
levelLines.36: Busy offices, quiet dome, side by side.
levelLines.37: The chain bends round the corner to the square.
levelLines.38: Every house in Wren Hollow. Starfall is on air.

town.caption: Downtown has two lamps on every roof.
The orchard farms are on air.
